title: Receipts
logline: On the day Corporate's auditor comes to decide Scranton's fate, Michael has no receipts, Dwight finds a form loophole, and Jim finally says the thing in a parking lot.
outline: A: Michael has no receipts for Gerald Boyd's review; he tries to win love before the count; staff vouch for him. B: Jim finally confesses to Pam; she says she can't; Jim requests the Stamford transfer. C: Dwight finds a form that makes him Assistant Regional Manager; Andy sulks, then they share a nod; Angela thanks Dwight in public. Order: cold, A, B, C, A, B, A, C, B, A, C, tag.
theme: Being seen by someone is not the same as being chosen by them.
storySoFar: Season finale. Corporate's auditor Gerald Boyd is reviewing Scranton's headcount and wants receipts; the office has written him secret letters praising Michael. Dwight is Acting RM by memo and in an armed truce with Andy, who came from Stamford with a better tie. Jim confessed to Pam in the parking lot; she said she can't, and did not say she doesn't feel it. Jim has requested a transfer to Stamford. Roy has cancelled again and finally sets a wedding date. Angela and Dwight's secret is known to Oscar and Kevin, who say nothing. Michael's Things I Love board holds Dwight's percentage, Kevin's M&Ms, Dale's card, and Pam's drawing of Michael running. Stanley's countdown is at 197.

stateChanges.status: Jim confessed in the parking lot; Pam said she can't and did not say she doesn't feel it; Jim requested Stamford transfer
armed truce renewed with a grudging nod; Dwight holds ARM title by form technicality

stateChanges.arc: Will They, Won't They: Jim and Pam
stateChanges.progress: Confession made and turned down for now; Jim transferring to Stamford; Pam's desk has a card from Jim
Headcount unchanged for now; Gerald wants receipts next quarter; Michael moved to tears by the office's letters
Dwight named Assistant Regional Manager by technicality; Andy sulks then nods; truce holds
Angela thanks Dwight publicly; Oscar and Kevin still say nothing

stateChanges.text: Roy set a wedding date: June 14. Pam received it in the tag along with Jim's card.
Gerald Boyd asked for receipts next quarter; the letters are on file.
Stanley's countdown: 198 in the cold open, 197 in the tag; Michael's 'That's what she said' lands on silence; Kevin: 'Nobody say nothing.'
Andy's bear-paw phone plays banjo hold music; Oscar: 'Actually, that's a banjo on hold.'

scenes.recap: Andy's banjo hold music plays while Stanley counts down and Michael's joke dies on silence.

beats.caption: holds up bear-paw phone as banjo hold music plays

beats.text: Actually, that's a banjo on hold.
It's a bluegrass hold. Very calming.
Stanley, how many days left?
That's what she said.

beats.caption: silence

beats.text: Nobody say nothing.

scenes.recap: Michael calls an emergency meeting about Gerald Boyd's receipts and gets no useful answers.

beats.text: Gerald Boyd, Corporate auditor, arrives at three o'clock. He is going to ask us for receipts.

lines: Gerald Boyd has the face of a closed Sbarro. I'm not scared. I'm a little scared. I'm also a little hungry.

beats.text: Question: What form of proof? Per my memo, all receipts are to be in triplicate.
Actually, Corporate receipts are invoices. Also, we have no receipts for anything in this branch.
Me have receipt for chili. Chili is proof.
I once had a receipt for a man. Nobody followed up.
Can I go home now.
No, Stanley! This is the most important day in the history of this branch.
We could sing Gerald the Cornell fight song. Nobody can be sad during the fight song.
We are not singing, Andy. We are being a family.

beats.caption: Andy takes off his tie to show his heart

beats.text: Pam, Jim, you two are on the welcome committee. Make it warm. Make it feel like a hug.
Sure, Michael.

scenes.recap: Jim asks Pam to talk after the review, and Pam wonders whether it's another prank.

beats.text: Hey. Can you come outside with me after the review?
Is this about the prank? Because Dwight already knows.
It's not a prank.
Everything's a prank with you.
Yeah. I know.

lines: Jim has been about to tell me something since August. I have been pretending I'm not waiting for it. I'm very good at pretending. It's my whole personality.

beats.text: Ooh, is this about Shannon? Because I heard he's basically engaged.
Kelly, no.

scenes.recap: Dwight discovers a form that calls him Assistant Regional Manager, and Andy calls it a typo.

beats.caption: reads the Corporate audit roster with a highlighter

beats.text: Question: Did you read Section Nine? The acting regional manager shall be listed as Assistant Regional Manager.
That's a typo, Dwight. A Corporate typo.
False. It is a typo that is now official. Forms are binding.
Actually, Andy, he's right. I checked the form. The form is wrong, and it's in ink.
Oscar, you're supposed to be on my side.
I'm on the side of the facts. Which is your side on Tuesdays.

beats.caption: Andy inhales, about to sing, and stops himself

scenes.recap: Michael shows Toby his receipt folder of napkins and asks if the office likes him.

beats.text: Toby, I need you to look at my receipts. Tell me they're receipts.

beats.caption: holds up a folder of napkins labeled RECEIPTS

beats.text: Michael, those are napkins from Chili's.
They are proof that I took people to lunch.

lines: Toby is the only person here I don't have to be funny for. That's why I hate him. Kidding. Not kidding. It's complicated, like a Ferris wheel.

beats.text: Do you think they like me?

beats.caption: Toby decides how honest to be

beats.text: ...Yes.
You said that like a hostage.
I've been in HR for fourteen years. I say everything like that.
Toby, at the review, tell Gerald the truth. That you think I'm good.
That's not in the fire code.

scenes.recap: Jim finally tells Pam how he feels in the parking lot, and Pam says she can't.

beats.text: You said outside. It's outside. Say it.
I like you, Pam. Not as a bit. Not as a prank. I've liked you since the day you were the only person who laughed at my joke.

beats.caption: a car alarm goes off somewhere

beats.text: Jim.
You don't have to say anything.
Roy—
I know about Roy.
I can't, Jim. I can't do this today.
I'm not saying I—

beats.caption: Pam doesn't finish the sentence

beats.text: Okay.

lines: I said it next to a dumpster. It's the most me thing I've ever done. She didn't say no. She just didn't say yes. I'm choosing to hear the first part.

beats.text: I'm going to ask Toby about the Stamford transfer.
Stamford.

scenes.recap: Gerald Boyd asks for receipts, the staff produces letters, and the headcount stays the same.

beats.text: Gerald! Welcome to the Scranton family. Dwight, get Gerald the good chair.
I need receipts, Michael.
Of course. Let me tell you about our receipts. They are feelings.
Feelings are not a receipt.
Michael. Good boss. Give me M&Ms.
Our receipts are sales figures, and also letters. Actually, many letters.
Yes. Fourteen letters. Each one uses the phrase 'Michael is a light in the dark.'
We used a template. Mine was in pencil.
I wrote one about being buried alive. I don't know what it means.

beats.caption: nobody follows up

beats.text: Headcount is unchanged. For now.
Unchanged?
Bring me receipts next quarter. Good day.
You guys wrote me letters?

beats.caption: stares at the stack of letters and can't speak

beats.text: Question: Are you crying?
I'm allergic to Gerald. Excuse me. I'm going to be in my office. Forever.

scenes.recap: Dwight shows Andy the form, Andy sulks about his tie, and they reach a grudging nod.

beats.text: Andy. Gerald signed the roster. Assistant Regional Manager.

beats.caption: sets down bear-paw phone; banjo hold music plays

beats.text: That's a typo, Dwight. Gerald probably signed it while sneezing.
False. Gerald does not sneeze. He sighs.
I came from Stamford with a better tie.
You do have a better tie.
Thank you. I'm going to sulk now.

beats.caption: slumps over table_4 with a bear-paw phone on his chest

beats.text: Sulk somewhere else. Some of us are on a break from you.
Andy. You keep the crowd. I keep the title.

beats.caption: Andy looks up

beats.text: ...Yeah. Okay. Good.

scenes.recap: Jim files his Stamford transfer with Toby, who says it isn't in the fire code and is sad about it.

beats.text: Toby, I need a transfer form. Stamford.
Stamford. Okay.
It's not in the fire code. But I'll file it.
Thanks, Toby.
Pam is going to miss you.
You think?
I think. I'm going to be sad about it at home. Alone. With the fire code.

beats.caption: types at reception and doesn't look up

beats.text: Don't tell Michael.
I'm not allowed to tell him things. He's not allowed to hear them.

scenes.recap: Michael finds the Things I Love board updated with new notes, and hides a tear behind a paper sample.

beats.caption: reads the Things I Love board, one note at a time

beats.text: Oscar wrote 'correct about forty percent of the time. Better than average.' That's a compliment.
It is a compliment. Also, I updated my note.
You wrote sixty-two percent.
I'm rounding up. Because you are a good boss.

lines: Michael is my boss. He is also the only person who has ever said I was good at something without a memo. Question: Do I cry? No. I have beet juice.

beats.text: Dwight. Are you going to say something nice?
Michael Scott, you are not the worst regional manager in the Northeast.

beats.caption: Michael raises a paper sample in front of his face

beats.text: Is that a paper sample?
It is a paper sample.
Okay. Thank you. Go away now. Forever.

scenes.recap: Angela thanks Dwight in public for checking the fax, and Oscar and Kevin say nothing.

beats.text: Dwight. Thank you for checking the Party Planning fax. It was adequate.
I am the Assistant Regional Manager. Checking faxes is my duty.
Of course you are. Your cuff is uneven, by the way.

beats.caption: straightens Dwight's cuff with two fingers, then walks away

beats.text: Nobody say nothing.
I'm not saying anything.

lines: I knew about the beets. I have known for weeks. I am not going to say it, because the moment I do, Angela will have me reassigned to the warehouse, and I cannot do Kevin's taxes alone.

scenes.recap: Pam finds Jim's card on her desk as Roy arrives with a wedding date, and Stanley's countdown hits 197.

beats.caption: finds a card on her desk, in handwriting she knows

beats.text: 'Some things are easier to say on paper. J.'
Babe. We set a date. June fourteenth. I booked the hall.
Roy, we—
Don't cry. It's the warehouse. It gets dusty.

beats.caption: slides Jim's card into her drawer

beats.text: One ninety-seven.
That's what she said.

beats.caption: silence

beats.text: Nobody say nothing.
